focus: Q5, where each proposed check belongs
noveltyJustification: Four findings are fully new (the per-change gate design, the weekly report's non-gating rationale, the pre-commit repair-on-commit contract, the missing template-render check); three consolidate placement and count as half new.
ruledOut: Adding a corpus-wide sweep to pre-commit
Making the weekly report a gate

label: The per-change gate is the right first line: changed-packet-validation.yml selects only packets whose own graded documents changed, validates --strict --no-recursive, blocks only regressions by comparing against a merge-base worktree, fails closed when no verdict is emitted, and installs the toolchain so a missing build cannot read as failing packets.

Whole-corpus visibility exists but is deliberately not a gate: the weekly strict-pass-freshness-report sweep reports only, with the rationale that a report misread as a gate is worse than none; it is the natural home for census output.
The advisory suite already runs the trigger-index freshness check without gating, so index staleness is reported on relevant changes and repaired by the rebuild workflow after merge.

The pre-commit hook already demonstrates repair-on-commit: it auto re-mints a packet's graph-metadata.json when staged documents change and blocks only when it cannot fix it, alongside route re-mint, mirror sync, comment hygiene and card-sync gates.

The pre-push hook owns volume and history gates: mass-deletion ceiling, remote-allowlist approval, route guard, per-ref track-root drift and commit-message templates; new checks over a whole pushed range belong there or in CI, not pre-commit.

Placement map: deterministic unit checks (scaffold-render anchor test, Gate 3 constants drift test, phrase-list single-source test) belong in the spec-kit suites spec-kit-check.yml runs; the corpus census belongs in the weekly freshness report or advisory; the applied-state audit and phrase-cleanup diff rule belong in CI advisory or pre-push; the sidecar staging and post-commit --check belong inside the rebuild workflow.

The cheapest check that would have caught the template anchor bug does not exist anywhere: no workflow or hook renders the templates and checks rendered anchor pairing, so the nesting shipped through every existing gate into every new scaffold.

direction: Adding a corpus-wide sweep to pre-commit
reason: The pre-commit contract is per-commit and fast; the derived-metadata re-mint is the ceiling of what belongs there.
